items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He said, “I want you to join the band tonight, as of now.”

ctx.x: And I’m like a kid. Come on. I’m so scared, I’m shaking in my boots. I’m doing a trio with Elvin Jones at Rudy Van Gelder’s, where Coltrane recorded with Elvin. I’m 25 years old. Anyway, you do the record. We did the record, whatever that after- – one day. He didn’t say anything to me. That’s it. By chance, two weeks later I did My Goal’s Beyond with [John] McLaughlin. That’s another story. I met him. But it’s February – January, February of ’70 or ’71, I do these two records, heavy records. I’m still with Ten…

“Joe’s leaving. You’re going to take Joe’s place.” He says, “So it’s going to be a transition period.” And in that next six months, Clifford Jordan, Frank Foster, and Joe. I would always be with one of them, sometimes with none of them, sometimes Jan Hammer. Chick played a little bit. But this was this transition period, until finally Joe was gone and Grossman came into the band. Somewhere 6, 9 months with Elvin, and eventually Don Alias. He was with us for a year. That’s the period with Elvin, which is a two,…

items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was doing a lot of record dates and all that so I got Steve Grossman and David Liebman, and Gene Perla.

ctx.x: Okay so let’s go back to, again, Jimmy Garrison is having some personal problems, which preclude him from continuing on in the Elvin Jones Trio. Who did you get to replace him?

Gene Clark, and after that Joe was, he was a little bit… He was doing a lot of record dates and all that so I got Steve Grossman and David Liebman, and Gene Perla. I still didn’t have a pianist (Laughs).

I’m holding in my hand a copy of “Poly Curtains” and this date is September 26th, a little after your birthday of that year in 1969 and this one has a composition entitled “Mr. Jones” this one has Joe Farrell and also George Coleman and Wilbur Little on bass and Condita on congas. This happened to be a particular favorite of mine. I just wanted to ask Keiko about “Mr. Jones” since that happen to be one of my favorites.
